subject: maths
title: Year 5 12- and 24-Hour Time
seo_title: Year 5 12- and 24-Hour Time Worksheets: Converting Time, Durations and Timetables (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and solve practical problems involving the conversion between them
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on 12- and 24-hour time for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5M03): read analog clocks to the minute, convert between am/pm and 24-hour time, work out how long events last and solve problems with Sydney train timetables, flights and TV guides. 100 questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: pm: add 12 to the hour. 3:45 pm = 15:45.
key_sub: am times keep the hour with 4 digits (7:05 am = 07:05). 12:20 pm = 12:20, but 12:20 am = 00:20. An hour has 60 minutes, so count on to the next o’clock to work out how long.
body_html:
Two ways to write the time

A day has 24 hours. An analog clock only shows 12, so 12-hour time adds am (midnight to midday) or pm (midday to midnight). 24-hour time counts the hours from 00 to 23, so it needs no am or pm. It always has 4 digits: 07:30, 15:45. Train timetables, flights and TV guides often use it.

12-hour to 24-hour

12-hour24-hourRule
12:20 am00:20just after midnight: the hour is 00
7:05 am07:05am: keep the hour, write 4 digits
12:20 pm12:20just after midday: keep 12
3:45 pm15:45pm: add 12 (3 + 12 = 15)
9:10 pm21:10pm: add 12 (9 + 12 = 21)
Analog to 24-hour

The clock shows 20 to 7 in the evening. Write it in 24-hour time.

20 to 7 is 40 minutes past 6: 6:40 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 6 + 12 = 18.

Answer: 18:40

24-hour to 12-hour

Hours 13 to 23: take away 12 and write pm. Hours 01 to 11: keep the hour and write am. 12 is pm and 00 is 12 am.

Read a timetable time

A train arrives at 17:08. Write it in 12-hour time.

17 − 12 = 5, and it is after midday.

Answer: 5:08 pm

How long? Count on in jumps

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers. Jump to the next o’clock, then on in whole hours, then to the end time.

Mixed times

A school excursion leaves at 9:40 am and gets back at 14:15. How long is it?

Change 9:40 am to 09:40. 09:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes, 10:00 to 14:00 is 4 hours, 14:00 to 14:15 is 15 minutes.

Answer: 4 hours 35 minutes

Through midnight

A New Year’s Eve harbour cruise leaves at 23:20 and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. What time does it finish?

23:20 + 40 minutes = 00:00 (midnight). 1 hour 50 minutes − 40 minutes = 1 hour 10 minutes. 00:00 + 1 hour 10 minutes = 01:10.

Answer: 01:10, which is 1:10 am

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3:45 pm written as 13:45Add 12, do not put a 1 in front: 3 + 12 = 15, so 15:45
15:45 read as 5:45 pmTake away 12, do not drop the 1: 15 − 12 = 3, so 3:45 pm
12:20 am written as 12:20Just after midnight is 00 in 24-hour time: 00:20
12:20 pm written as 00:20 or 24:20Just after midday stays 12: 12:20
7:05 am written as 7:05 in 24-hour time24-hour time has 4 digits: 07:05
14:35 to 16:10 worked out as 1610 − 1435 = 1 hour 75 minutesCount on: 25 minutes + 1 hour + 10 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes

faq.q: When do students learn 24-hour time in Australia?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum v9.0, Year 5 students compare the 12- and 24-hour time systems and convert between them to solve practical problems (AC9M5M03). They read analog clocks to the nearest minute from Year 3.

faq.q: How do you change 12-hour time into 24-hour time?
faq.a: For am times keep the hour and write 4 digits, so 7:05 am is 07:05. For pm times add 12 to the hour, so 3:45 pm is 15:45. 12:20 pm stays 12:20 and 12:20 am becomes 00:20.
Midnight at the start of a day is written 00:00, so 12:20 am is 00:20. Some timetables write 24:00 for the very end of a day, but 00:00 is the usual way.

faq.q: Where is 24-hour time used in Australia?
faq.a: You see 24-hour time on train and bus timetables, airline tickets and flight boards, TV guides, phones and in hospitals. Practising with real timetables helps students with NAPLAN-style time problems.

The hour hand is between 10 and 11, so the hour is still 10. The minute hand points to 8: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 10:40 am.

The hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The minute hand is 1 small mark past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 16 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 9:16 am.

The hour hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is still 4. The minute hand is 2 small marks past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 37 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 4:37 pm.

items.q: Write 17 minutes to 4 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “17 minutes to 4” means 17 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 17 = 43, so it is 3:43. In the afternoon is pm, so it is 3:43 pm.

items.q: Write 22 minutes to 9 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “22 minutes to 9” means 22 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 22 = 38, so it is 8:38. In the morning is am, so it is 8:38 am.

items.q: Write 12 minutes past 7 in the evening as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “12 minutes past 7” means 12 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:12. In the evening is pm, so it is 7:12 pm.

items.q: Write 8 minutes to 12 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “8 minutes to 12” means 8 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 8 = 52, so it is 11:52. In the morning is am, so it is 11:52 am.

items.q: Write 2:20 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 2 + 12 = 14. So 2:20 pm is 14:20. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 12:20 is 12:20 pm.)

items.q: Write 6:55 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 6 + 12 = 18. So 6:55 pm is 18:55. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 16:55 is 4:55 pm.)

items.q: Write 6:40 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 6:40 am is 06:40.

items.q: Write 7:35 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 7:35 am is 07:35.

items.q: Write 11:20 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 11 + 12 = 23. So 11:20 pm is 23:20.

items.q: Write 9:05 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So 9:05 pm is 21:05. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 19:05 is 7:05 pm.)

items.q: Write 10:20 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. Do not add 12. 10:20 am is 10:20.

items.q: Write 12:30 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: 12 pm is the hour just after midday. Midday is 12:00 in 24-hour time, so do not add 12. 12:30 pm is 12:30.

items.q: Write 12:10 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: 12 am is the hour just after midnight. In 24-hour time a new day starts at 00:00, so 12:10 am is 00:10.

items.q: Write 10:13 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 10 + 12 = 22. So 10:13 pm is 22:13.

items.q: Write 5:56 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 5 + 12 = 17. So 5:56 pm is 17:56. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 15:56 is 3:56 pm.)

items.q: Write 3:39 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3:39 pm is 15:39. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 13:39 is 1:39 pm.)

items.q: Write 9:58 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 9:58 am is 09:58.

items.q: Write 11:36 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. Do not add 12. 11:36 am is 11:36.

items.q: Write 12:11 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: 12 pm is just after midday, and midday is 12:00. Keep the 12: 12:11.

items.q: Write 12:22 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: 12 am is just after midnight. The 24-hour clock starts the day at 00, so 12:22 am is 00:22.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is quarter to 8 in the evening?
items.e: “quarter to 8” is 15 minutes before 8 o’clock: 7:45 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 7 + 12 = 19. So it is 19:45.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is 25 past 4 in the afternoon?
items.e: “25 past 4” is 4:25 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 4 + 12 = 16. So it is 16:25.

The hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 48 minutes past. It is 8:48 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 8 + 12 = 20. So it is 20:48.

The hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. The minute hand is 3 small marks past the 1. Count in 5s to 5, then on in 1s: 8 minutes past. It is 1:08 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 1 + 12 = 13. So it is 13:08.

items.q: Write 15:15 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 15 − 12 = 3. So 15:15 is 3:15 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 5:15 pm is 17:15.)

items.q: Write 13:30 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 13 − 12 = 1. So 13:30 is 1:30 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 3:30 pm is 15:30.)

items.q: Write 06:35 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: The hour 06 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: am. Drop the 0 at the front: 6:35 am.

items.q: Write 09:30 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: The hour 09 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: am. Drop the 0 at the front: 9:30 am.

items.q: Write 18:35 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 18 − 12 = 6. So 18:35 is 6:35 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 8:35 pm is 20:35.)

items.q: Write 22:25 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 22 − 12 = 10. So 22:25 is 10:25 pm. (Take away 12, not 10: 12:25 pm is 12:25.)

items.q: Write 11:25 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: The hour 11 is less than 12, so it is a morning time. Keep the hour and write am: 11:25 am.

items.q: Write 12:05 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: 12 is the hour just after midday, so it is pm. Do not take away 12. 12:05 is 12:05 pm.

items.q: Write 00:25 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: 00 is the hour just after midnight. In 12-hour time we call it 12 am. 00:25 is 12:25 am.

items.q: Jack’s train leaves at 17:52. What is this in 12-hour time?
items.e: 17 is more than 12, so it is pm. 17 − 12 = 5. 17:52 is 5:52 pm. (Dropping the 1 gives 7:52 pm, which is 19:52.)

items.q: The koala talk at the wildlife park starts at 14:15. What is this in 12-hour time?
items.e: 14 − 12 = 2, and it is after midday, so it is pm. 14:15 is 2:15 pm.

items.q: Write 21:07 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 21 − 12 = 9. So 21:07 is 9:07 pm. (Take away 12, not 10: 11:07 pm is 23:07.)

items.q: Write 16:36 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 16 − 12 = 4. So 16:36 is 4:36 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 6:36 pm is 18:36.)

items.q: Write 19:24 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 19 − 12 = 7. So 19:24 is 7:24 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 9:24 pm is 21:24.)

items.q: Write 05:24 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: The hour 05 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: am. Drop the 0 at the front: 5:24 am.

items.q: Write 10:37 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: The hour 10 is less than 12, so it is a morning time. Keep the hour and write am: 10:37 am.

items.q: Write 12:22 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: 12 is just after midday, so it is pm. Keep the 12: 12:22 pm.

items.q: Write 00:02 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: 00 is the first hour of the day, just after midnight. In 12-hour time it is 12 am: 12:02 am.

items.q: Which of these times is the latest in the day?
items.e: Change them all to 24-hour time: 9:15 pm = 21:15, 11:05 am = 11:05. 11:05, 18:30, 20:50, 21:15. The latest is 9:15 pm.

items.q: Which of these times is the earliest in the day?
items.e: Change them all to 24-hour time: 12:40 am = 00:40, 1:15 am = 01:15, 12:10 pm = 12:10. The day starts at 00:00, so the earliest is 12:40 am.

sets.title: How long? Durations across 12- and 24-hour times

items.q: How long is it from 17:55 to 18:05?
items.e: Count on: 17:55 to 18:00 is 5 minutes, 18:00 to 18:05 is 5 minutes. 5 minutes + 5 minutes = 10 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 20:45 to 21:20?
items.e: Count on: 20:45 to 21:00 is 15 minutes, 21:00 to 21:20 is 20 minutes. 15 minutes + 20 minutes = 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 11:35 to 12:10?
items.e: Count on: 11:35 to 12:00 is 25 minutes, 12:00 to 12:10 is 10 minutes. 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 20:34 to 21:12?
items.e: Count on: 20:34 to 21:00 is 26 minutes, 21:00 to 21:12 is 12 minutes. 26 minutes + 12 minutes = 38 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 15:36 to 16:26?
items.e: Count on: 15:36 to 16:00 is 24 minutes, 16:00 to 16:26 is 26 minutes. 24 minutes + 26 minutes = 50 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 18:33 to 19:13?
items.e: Count on: 18:33 to 19:00 is 27 minutes, 19:00 to 19:13 is 13 minutes. 27 minutes + 13 minutes = 40 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 14:30 to 17:20?
items.e: Count on: 14:30 to 15:00 is 30 minutes, 15:00 to 17:00 is 2 hours, 17:00 to 17:20 is 20 minutes. 2 hours + 30 minutes + 20 minutes = 2 hours 50 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 10:45 to 14:05?
items.e: Count on: 10:45 to 11:00 is 15 minutes, 11:00 to 14:00 is 3 hours, 14:00 to 14:05 is 5 minutes. 3 hours + 15 minutes + 5 minutes = 3 hours 20 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 11:48 to 15:07?
items.e: Count on: 11:48 to 12:00 is 12 minutes, 12:00 to 15:00 is 3 hours, 15:00 to 15:07 is 7 minutes. 3 hours + 12 minutes + 7 minutes = 3 hours 19 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 17:52 to 21:30?
items.e: Count on: 17:52 to 18:00 is 8 minutes, 18:00 to 21:00 is 3 hours, 21:00 to 21:30 is 30 minutes. 3 hours + 8 minutes + 30 minutes = 3 hours 38 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 11:35 am to 2:25 pm?
items.e: Count on: 11:35 am to 12:00 pm is 25 minutes, 12:00 pm to 2:00 pm is 2 hours, 2:00 pm to 2:25 pm is 25 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 25 minutes = 2 hours 50 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 10:25 am to 3:15 pm?
items.e: Count on: 10:25 am to 11:00 am is 35 minutes, 11:00 am to 3:00 pm is 4 hours, 3:00 pm to 3:15 pm is 15 minutes. 4 hours + 35 minutes + 15 minutes = 4 hours 50 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 9:40 am to 2:35 pm?
items.e: Count on: 9:40 am to 10:00 am is 20 minutes, 10:00 am to 2:00 pm is 4 hours, 2:00 pm to 2:35 pm is 35 minutes. 4 hours + 20 minutes + 35 minutes = 4 hours 55 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 8:50 am to 13:25?
items.e: Change both times to 24-hour time first: 08:50 and 13:25. Count on: 08:50 to 09:00 is 10 minutes, 09:00 to 13:00 is 4 hours, 13:00 to 13:25 is 25 minutes. 4 hours + 10 minutes + 25 minutes = 4 hours 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 11:40 to 4:15 pm?
items.e: Change both times to 24-hour time first: 11:40 and 16:15. Count on: 11:40 to 12:00 is 20 minutes, 12:00 to 16:00 is 4 hours, 16:00 to 16:15 is 15 minutes. 4 hours + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 4 hours 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A junior cricket match starts at 14:35 and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: Add the hours first: 14:35 + 1 hour = 15:35. Then add 50 minutes: 15:35 to 16:00 is 25 minutes, 16:00 to 16:25 is 25 minutes. So it is 16:25.

items.q: The Year 5 excursion bus leaves school at 09:48. The trip to the zoo takes 2 hours 15 minutes. What time does it get there?
items.e: Add the hours first: 09:48 + 2 hours = 11:48. Then add 15 minutes: 11:48 to 12:00 is 12 minutes, 12:00 to 12:03 is 3 minutes. So it is 12:03.

items.q: The school concert starts at 19:50 and lasts 1 hour 15 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: Add the hours first: 19:50 + 1 hour = 20:50. Then add 15 minutes: 20:50 to 21:00 is 10 minutes, 21:00 to 21:05 is 5 minutes. So it is 21:05.

items.q: A movie finishes at 16:20. It is 1 hour 45 minutes long. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back the hours first: 16:20 − 1 hour = 15:20. Then count back 45 minutes: 14:35.

items.q: The athletics carnival breaks for lunch at 12:10. The morning events took 1 hour 35 minutes. What time did they start?
items.e: Count back the hours first: 12:10 − 1 hour = 11:10. Then count back 35 minutes: 10:35.

sets.title: Timetables and time problems: trains, flights and TV

items.q: A train leaves Central at 17:14. What time does it get to Parramatta?
items.e: Find 17:14 in the Central row. Go down that column to the Parramatta row: 17:42.

items.q: A train gets to Strathfield at 17:43. What time did it leave Central?
items.e: Find 17:43 in the Strathfield row. Go up that column to the Central row: 17:29.

items.q: How long does the train that leaves Central at 16:44 take to get to Parramatta?
items.e: Count on: 16:44 to 17:00 is 16 minutes, 17:00 to 17:12 is 12 minutes. 16 minutes + 12 minutes = 28 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Chloe must be at Parramatta by 17:50. What is the latest train she can catch from Redfern?
items.e: Look along the Parramatta row for the last time that is not after 17:50: 17:42. Go up that column to Redfern: 17:17. The next train gets to Parramatta at 17:57, which is too late.

items.q: Leo gets to Redfern at 17:10, just after a train has left. How long must he wait for the next one?
items.e: The 17:02 train has gone. The next train from Redfern is at 17:17. Count on: 17:10 to 17:17 is 7 minutes. So it is 7 minutes.

items.q: Oliver’s train gets to Strathfield at 5:28 pm. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 5:28 pm is after midday, so add 12 to the hour: 5 + 12 = 17. Look for 17:28 in the Strathfield row.

items.q: A Friday night footy match starts at 19:25. With the breaks it lasts 2 hours 40 minutes. What time does it finish, in 12-hour time?
items.e: 19:25 + 2 hours = 21:25. Then add 40 minutes: 35 minutes takes it to 22:00, then 5 more: 22:05. 22 − 12 = 10, so it finishes at 10:05 pm.

items.q: The swimming carnival starts at 9:35 am and finishes at 14:20. How long does it last?
items.e: Change 9:35 am to 09:35. Count on: 09:35 to 10:00 is 25 minutes, 10:00 to 14:00 is 4 hours, 14:00 to 14:20 is 20 minutes. 4 hours + 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 4 hours 45 minutes. (14:20 is 2:20 pm, not 4:20 pm.)

items.q: How long is the flight from Melbourne to Hobart?
items.e: Count on: 09:55 to 10:00 is 5 minutes, 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour, 11:00 to 11:10 is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 5 minutes + 10 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Which flight takes the shortest time?
items.e: Work out each flight: Sydney to Melbourne 1 hour 30 minutes, Melbourne to Hobart 1 hour 15 minutes, Sydney to Canberra 55 minutes, Melbourne to Sydney 1 hour 25 minutes. The shortest is Sydney to Canberra.

items.q: Zara flies from Melbourne to Sydney. What time does she land, in 12-hour time?
items.e: The flight arrives at 19:10. 19 − 12 = 7, and it is the evening, so it is 7:10 pm.

items.q: The flight from Sydney to Canberra is 45 minutes late. What time does it land now?
items.e: It was going to land at 14:20. 14:20 + 45 minutes: 40 minutes takes it to 15:00, then 5 more minutes: 15:05.

items.q: Mei gets to the pool at 5:10 pm. The sign says the pool closes at 17:45. How long can she swim?
Dinner is at 18:30. A roast takes 1 hour 45 minutes to cook. What time must it go in the oven?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 18:30 − 1 hour = 17:30. Then count back 45 minutes: 30 minutes to 17:00, then 15 more: 16:45.

items.q: Which program is on at 8:15 pm?
items.e: 8:15 pm is 20:15 in 24-hour time (8 + 12 = 20). The documentary starts at 19:30 and the movie starts at 20:45, so the Wildlife documentary is on. (8:15 pm is not 18:15.)

items.q: The movie runs until the late news starts. How long is the movie?
items.e: Count on: 20:45 to 21:00 is 15 minutes, 21:00 to 23:00 is 2 hours, 23:00 to 23:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Matilda’s bedtime is 9:30 pm. How much of the movie can she watch before bed?
items.e: 9:30 pm is 21:30. Count on: 20:45 to 21:00 is 15 minutes, 21:00 to 21:30 is 30 minutes. 15 minutes + 30 minutes = 45 minutes.

items.q: What time does the Late news start, in 12-hour time?
items.e: The late news starts at 23:10. 23 − 12 = 11, and it is night, so it is 11:10 pm. (Dropping the 2 gives 3:10 pm, which is 15:10.)

items.q: An overnight train leaves Sydney at 20:40 and gets to Melbourne at 07:35 the next morning. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 20:40 to 21:00 is 20 minutes, 21:00 to 07:00 is 10 hours, 07:00 to 07:35 is 35 minutes. 10 hours + 20 minutes + 35 minutes = 10 hours 55 minutes. (Taking 07:35 from 20:40 gives 13 hours 5 minutes, but the train travels through midnight.)

items.q: Ruby’s mum parks at 11:55 am and pays for 2 hours 30 minutes. By what time must she leave, in 24-hour time?
items.e: 11:55 + 2 hours = 13:55. Then add 30 minutes: 5 minutes takes it to 14:00, then 25 more: 14:25. It is after midday, so the hour is 14, not 02.
